count_semantics_notes: CDPH WNV reports typically distinguish neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive human cases; map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed, non-neuroinvasive to cases_probable or cases_confirmed per case definition.
ArboNET uses 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CSTE case definitions: confirmed = lab-confirmed (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable = IgM in serum with compatible illness.
Cumulative season-to-date figures are common; extract the specific August 2024 increment or clearly flag if figures are cumulative YTD.
County-level breakdowns may be available in CDPH weekly WNV updates; prioritize county-level rows over statewide aggregates when both are present.
Death counts in WNV reports may lag case counts by weeks; note reporting lag in evidence_quote.
Sentinel chicken seroconversions and dead bird positives are NOT human case counts; exclude from case_count fields but note in evidence_quote if contextually relevant.
Some CDPH tables report 'human cases' as a combined confirmed+probable figure; record in cases_unspecified if disaggregation is unavailable.
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH WNV updates; record as null if absent rather than zero.
disambiguation_risks: WNV animal/veterinary cases (horses, birds) must not be counted as human cases
Sentinel chicken seroconversions are surveillance indicators, not human cases
Dead bird reports are epizootic indicators, not human cases
Mosquito pool positivity rates are vector data, not human case counts
West Nile virus vs. other California arboviruses (St. Louis encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalomyelitis virus, dengue, Zika) — confirm pathogen identity
Cumulative YTD figures vs. August-specific figures — clearly distinguish time window
WNND (neuroinvasive) vs. WNF (non-neuroinvasive) — do not conflate clinical categories unless source aggregates them
California county names may be ambiguous (e.g., 'Orange' county vs. city of Orange) — always record full county name with 'County' suffix
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates; filter to California-specific rows only

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for West Nile Virus Disease from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus weekly or monthly surveillance reports covering August 2024, containing human case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human surveillance in California and publishes weekly WNV activity reports during the transmission season. These are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, and unspecified human case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county and local health department (LHD) WNV situation reports, press releases, or dashboards for August 2024 covering high-burden counties (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno, Kern, San Joaquin, Riverside, San Bernardino).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County-level LHDs often publish localized WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than state-level reports. High-burden California counties are historically the primary contributors to statewide WNV case totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance data for California for 2024, including any state-level or county-level human case and death counts reportable for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case data. CDC DVBD may publish weekly or cumulative WNV maps and tables that include California-specific counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., CDC WNV disease data, ProMED, HealthMap, or open data portals) that aggregate California WNV human case counts for 2024 for cross-validation against CDPH primary sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators provide a held-back validation layer to detect discrepancies in case counts, death totals, or reporting periods between primary and secondary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO or ECDC situation reports or global arboviral surveillance summaries that include United States or California WNV data for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports may independently summarize US WNV activity and provide a secondary validation reference for California case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definitions for West Nile virus confirmed, probable, and suspected human cases to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WNV case definitions distinguish neuroinvasive disease (WNND) from West Nile fever (WNF) and affect how confirmed vs. probable counts should be interpreted and mapped to schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV transmission season patterns, historical burden, and 2024 season context to support interpretation of August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Contextual literature helps assess whether August 2024 counts are within expected seasonal ranges and supports normalization decisions for cumulative vs. incident count semantics.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report cumulative year-to-date WNV counts without a clear August 2024 incident period breakdown, or that mix human and animal/vector surveillance data, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Cumulative YTD counts may not be attributable to the August 2024 window alone. Mixed human/animal data violates the task acceptance contract exclusion terms and must be reviewed before any extraction attempt.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite WNV case counts without a clearly identified primary official source, for human review to assess provenance reliability.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may cite unofficial or unverified counts. Without traceable provenance to an official agency, such records require human review before entering the collection pipeline.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH WNV reports typically distinguish neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive human cases; map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed, non-neuroinvasive to cases_probable or cases_confirmed per case definition.
ArboNET uses 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CSTE case definitions: confirmed = lab-confirmed (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable = IgM in serum with compatible illness.
Cumulative season-to-date figures are common; extract the specific August 2024 increment or clearly flag if figures are cumulative YTD.
County-level breakdowns may be available in CDPH weekly WNV updates; prioritize county-level rows over statewide aggregates when both are present.
Death counts in WNV reports may lag case counts by weeks; note reporting lag in evidence_quote.
Sentinel chicken seroconversions and dead bird positives are NOT human case counts; exclude from case_count fields but note in evidence_quote if contextually relevant.
Some CDPH tables report 'human cases' as a combined confirmed+probable figure; record in cases_unspecified if disaggregation is unavailable.
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH WNV updates; record as null if absent rather than zero.
disambiguation_risks: WNV animal/veterinary cases (horses, birds) must not be counted as human cases
Sentinel chicken seroconversions are surveillance indicators, not human cases
Dead bird reports are epizootic indicators, not human cases
Mosquito pool positivity rates are vector data, not human case counts
West Nile virus vs. other California arboviruses (St. Louis encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalomyelitis virus, dengue, Zika) — confirm pathogen identity
Cumulative YTD figures vs. August-specific figures — clearly distinguish time window
WNND (neuroinvasive) vs. WNF (non-neuroinvasive) — do not conflate clinical categories unless source aggregates them
California county names may be ambiguous (e.g., 'Orange' county vs. city of Orange) — always record full county name with 'County' suffix
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates; filter to California-specific rows only

core_fields.name: subnational_location

core_fields.name: event_start_date

core_fields.name: event_end_date

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH WNV reports typically distinguish neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive human cases; map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed, non-neuroinvasive to cases_probable or cases_confirmed per case definition.
ArboNET uses 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CSTE case definitions: confirmed = lab-confirmed (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable = IgM in serum with compatible illness.
Cumulative season-to-date figures are common; extract the specific August 2024 increment or clearly flag if figures are cumulative YTD.
County-level breakdowns may be available in CDPH weekly WNV updates; prioritize county-level rows over statewide aggregates when both are present.
Death counts in WNV reports may lag case counts by weeks; note reporting lag in evidence_quote.
Sentinel chicken seroconversions and dead bird positives are NOT human case counts; exclude from case_count fields but note in evidence_quote if contextually relevant.
Some CDPH tables report 'human cases' as a combined confirmed+probable figure; record in cases_unspecified if disaggregation is unavailable.
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH WNV updates; record as null if absent rather than zero.
disambiguation_risks: WNV animal/veterinary cases (horses, birds) must not be counted as human cases
Sentinel chicken seroconversions are surveillance indicators, not human cases
Dead bird reports are epizootic indicators, not human cases
Mosquito pool positivity rates are vector data, not human case counts
West Nile virus vs. other California arboviruses (St. Louis encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalomyelitis virus, dengue, Zika) — confirm pathogen identity
Cumulative YTD figures vs. August-specific figures — clearly distinguish time window
WNND (neuroinvasive) vs. WNF (non-neuroinvasive) — do not conflate clinical categories unless source aggregates them
California county names may be ambiguous (e.g., 'Orange' county vs. city of Orange) — always record full county name with 'County' suffix
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates; filter to California-specific rows only

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus weekly or monthly surveillance reports covering August 2024, containing human case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human surveillance in California and publishes weekly WNV activity reports during the transmission season. These are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, and unspecified human case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county and local health department (LHD) WNV situation reports, press releases, or dashboards for August 2024 covering high-burden counties (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno, Kern, San Joaquin, Riverside, San Bernardino).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County-level LHDs often publish localized WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than state-level reports. High-burden California counties are historically the primary contributors to statewide WNV case totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance data for California for 2024, including any state-level or county-level human case and death counts reportable for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case data. CDC DVBD may publish weekly or cumulative WNV maps and tables that include California-specific counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., CDC WNV disease data, ProMED, HealthMap, or open data portals) that aggregate California WNV human case counts for 2024 for cross-validation against CDPH primary sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators provide a held-back validation layer to detect discrepancies in case counts, death totals, or reporting periods between primary and secondary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO or ECDC situation reports or global arboviral surveillance summaries that include United States or California WNV data for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports may independently summarize US WNV activity and provide a secondary validation reference for California case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definitions for West Nile virus confirmed, probable, and suspected human cases to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WNV case definitions distinguish neuroinvasive disease (WNND) from West Nile fever (WNF) and affect how confirmed vs. probable counts should be interpreted and mapped to schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV transmission season patterns, historical burden, and 2024 season context to support interpretation of August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Contextual literature helps assess whether August 2024 counts are within expected seasonal ranges and supports normalization decisions for cumulative vs. incident count semantics.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report cumulative year-to-date WNV counts without a clear August 2024 incident period breakdown, or that mix human and animal/vector surveillance data, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Cumulative YTD counts may not be attributable to the August 2024 window alone. Mixed human/animal data violates the task acceptance contract exclusion terms and must be reviewed before any extraction attempt.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite WNV case counts without a clearly identified primary official source, for human review to assess provenance reliability.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may cite unofficial or unverified counts. Without traceable provenance to an official agency, such records require human review before entering the collection pipeline.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Division of Communicable Disease Control publishes weekly West Nile virus activity reports during the California transmission season (typically May–November), including human case counts by county, disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. fever), deaths, and hospitalizations. California county and city health departments (58 LHDs) may publish localized WNV human case data. CDC DVBD and ArboNET publish state-level human WNV surveillance data. These are the highest-priority extractable sourc...[truncated]

CDC ArboNET structured data tables, CDC WNV disease data open datasets, California open data portals, and HealthMap/ProMED aggregated surveillance databases may provide independently structured California WNV human case counts for cross-validation. These sources are held back from primary extraction and used to validate collection-source records.

WHO, PAHO, and ECDC may publish global or regional arboviral surveillance summaries that include US WNV activity data for 2024. These provide an independent international validation layer for California case and death totals.

Reputable California news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and public health news services (e.g., CIDRAP, ProMED) may report WNV human case counts, deaths, or outbreak alerts for California in August 2024, often citing CDPH or county LHD data. Useful as collection support when official sources are not yet indexed or accessible.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV transmission, case definitions, historical burden, and 2024 season context support interpretation and normalization of extracted counts. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific incident data due to publication lag, but valuable for case definition and count semantics context.

Their annual or weekly WNV activity reports will contain confirmed/probable case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns for 2024, including the August window. Using agency name + disease + year in natural language is more likely to surface the correct landing page than rigid exact-phrase matching.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH West Nile virus surveillance page, annual summary, or weekly activity report for 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdph.ca.gov domain; official state agency authorship; tabular case counts by county and week

query_batch.query: CDC West Nile virus 2024 California cases ArboNET surveillance statistics
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC's ArboNET system is the national arboviral surveillance database and publishes state-level WNV case counts including California. The CDC WNV activity page is updated regularly during transmission season and will contain confirmed neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts, deaths, and state breakdowns for 2024. This is a critical cross-validation source against CDPH data.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC WNV activity and surveillance data page or ArboNET state-level table for 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; ArboNET attribution; tabular state-by-state case counts

This query targets county-level official sources for August 2024 specifically.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH WNV reports typically distinguish neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive human cases; map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed, non-neuroinvasive to cases_probable or cases_confirmed per case definition.
ArboNET uses 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CSTE case definitions: confirmed = lab-confirmed (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable = IgM in serum with compatible illness.
Cumulative season-to-date figures are common; extract the specific August 2024 increment or clearly flag if figures are cumulative YTD.
County-level breakdowns may be available in CDPH weekly WNV updates; prioritize county-level rows over statewide aggregates when both are present.
Death counts in WNV reports may lag case counts by weeks; note reporting lag in evidence_quote.
Sentinel chicken seroconversions and dead bird positives are NOT human case counts; exclude from case_count fields but note in evidence_quote if contextually relevant.
Some CDPH tables report 'human cases' as a combined confirmed+probable figure; record in cases_unspecified if disaggregation is unavailable.
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH WNV updates; record as null if absent rather than zero.
disambiguation_risks: WNV animal/veterinary cases (horses, birds) must not be counted as human cases
Sentinel chicken seroconversions are surveillance indicators, not human cases

Mosquito pool positivity rates are vector data, not human case counts
West Nile virus vs. other California arboviruses (St. Louis encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalomyelitis virus, dengue, Zika) — confirm pathogen identity
Cumulative YTD figures vs. August-specific figures — clearly distinguish time window
WNND (neuroinvasive) vs. WNF (non-neuroinvasive) — do not conflate clinical categories unless source aggregates them
California county names may be ambiguous (e.g., 'Orange' county vs. city of Orange) — always record full county name with 'County' suffix
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates; filter to California-specific rows only

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus weekly or monthly surveillance reports covering August 2024, containing human case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human surveillance in California and publishes weekly WNV activity reports during the transmission season. These are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, and unspecified human case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county and local health department (LHD) WNV situation reports, press releases, or dashboards for August 2024 covering high-burden counties (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno, Kern, San Joaquin, Riverside, San Bernardino).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County-level LHDs often publish localized WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than state-level reports. High-burden California counties are historically the primary contributors to statewide WNV case totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance data for California for 2024, including any state-level or county-level human case and death counts reportable for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case data. CDC DVBD may publish weekly or cumulative WNV maps and tables that include California-specific counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., CDC WNV disease data, ProMED, HealthMap, or open data portals) that aggregate California WNV human case counts for 2024 for cross-validation against CDPH primary sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators provide a held-back validation layer to detect discrepancies in case counts, death totals, or reporting periods between primary and secondary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO or ECDC situation reports or global arboviral surveillance summaries that include United States or California WNV data for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports may independently summarize US WNV activity and provide a secondary validation reference for California case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definitions for West Nile virus confirmed, probable, and suspected human cases to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WNV case definitions distinguish neuroinvasive disease (WNND) from West Nile fever (WNF) and affect how confirmed vs. probable counts should be interpreted and mapped to schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV transmission season patterns, historical burden, and 2024 season context to support interpretation of August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Contextual literature helps assess whether August 2024 counts are within expected seasonal ranges and supports normalization decisions for cumulative vs. incident count semantics.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report cumulative year-to-date WNV counts without a clear August 2024 incident period breakdown, or that mix human and animal/vector surveillance data, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Cumulative YTD counts may not be attributable to the August 2024 window alone. Mixed human/animal data violates the task acceptance contract exclusion terms and must be reviewed before any extraction attempt.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite WNV case counts without a clearly identified primary official source, for human review to assess provenance reliability.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus weekly or monthly surveillance reports covering August 2024, containing human case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human surveillance in California and publishes weekly WNV activity reports during the transmission season. These are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, and unspecified human case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county and local health department (LHD) WNV situation reports, press releases, or dashboards for August 2024 covering high-burden counties (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno, Kern, San Joaquin, Riverside, San Bernardino).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County-level LHDs often publish localized WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than state-level reports. High-burden California counties are historically the primary contributors to statewide WNV case totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance data for California for 2024, including any state-level or county-level human case and death counts reportable for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case data. CDC DVBD may publish weekly or cumulative WNV maps and tables that include California-specific counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., CDC WNV disease data, ProMED, HealthMap, or open data portals) that aggregate California WNV human case counts for 2024 for cross-validation against CDPH primary sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators provide a held-back validation layer to detect discrepancies in case counts, death totals, or reporting periods between primary and secondary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO or ECDC situation reports or global arboviral surveillance summaries that include United States or California WNV data for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports may independently summarize US WNV activity and provide a secondary validation reference for California case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definitions for West Nile virus confirmed, probable, and suspected human cases to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WNV case definitions distinguish neuroinvasive disease (WNND) from West Nile fever (WNF) and affect how confirmed vs. probable counts should be interpreted and mapped to schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV transmission season patterns, historical burden, and 2024 season context to support interpretation of August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Contextual literature helps assess whether August 2024 counts are within expected seasonal ranges and supports normalization decisions for cumulative vs. incident count semantics.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report cumulative year-to-date WNV counts without a clear August 2024 incident period breakdown, or that mix human and animal/vector surveillance data, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Cumulative YTD counts may not be attributable to the August 2024 window alone. Mixed human/animal data violates the task acceptance contract exclusion terms and must be reviewed before any extraction attempt.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite WNV case counts without a clearly identified primary official source, for human review to assess provenance reliability.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may cite unofficial or unverified counts. Without traceable provenance to an official agency, such records require human review before entering the collection pipeline.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Division of Communicable Disease Control publishes weekly West Nile virus activity reports during the California transmission season (typically May–November), including human case counts by county, disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. fever), deaths, and hospitalizations. California county and city health departments (58 LHDs) may publish localized WNV human case data. CDC DVBD and ArboNET publish state-level human WNV surveillance data. These are the highest-priority extractable sourc...[truncated]

CDC ArboNET structured data tables, CDC WNV disease data open datasets, California open data portals, and HealthMap/ProMED aggregated surveillance databases may provide independently structured California WNV human case counts for cross-validation. These sources are held back from primary extraction and used to validate collection-source records.

WHO, PAHO, and ECDC may publish global or regional arboviral surveillance summaries that include US WNV activity data for 2024. These provide an independent international validation layer for California case and death totals.

Reputable California news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and public health news services (e.g., CIDRAP, ProMED) may report WNV human case counts, deaths, or outbreak alerts for California in August 2024, often citing CDPH or county LHD data. Useful as collection support when official sources are not yet indexed or accessible.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV transmission, case definitions, historical burden, and 2024 season context support interpretation and normalization of extracted counts. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific incident data due to publication lag, but valuable for case definition and count semantics context.

query_batch.query_rationale: CDPH is the primary authoritative source for statewide WNV surveillance in California. Their annual or weekly WNV activity reports will contain confirmed/probable case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns for 2024, including the August window. Using agency name + disease + year in natural language is more likely to surface the correct landing page than rigid exact-phrase matching.

query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdph.ca.gov domain; official state agency authorship; tabular case counts by county and week

query_batch.query: CDC West Nile virus 2024 California cases ArboNET surveillance statistics

This is a critical cross-validation source against CDPH data.

trust_considerations: Prefer sources with explicit .gov or .ca.gov domains for case count data
CDPH and CDC are tier-1 authoritative sources; county health departments are tier-2
News articles are acceptable as collection support only if they cite a named official source or agency report with specific numeric figures
Avoid sources that aggregate or repackage data without citing primary agency — these should not be used as primary evidence
CDC ArboNET data may lag real-time by several weeks; CDPH weekly reports are more timely for the August 2024 window

WNV case classification in California follows CDC ArboNET case definitions: neuroinvasive disease (confirmed) vs. non-neuroinvasive (confirmed) vs. probable — queries should surface sources that distinguish these categories
search_iteration_plans.stop_condition_hypothesis: Iteration 1 is sufficient if results surface: (1) a CDPH WNV surveillance page or weekly/annual report with August 2024 case counts; (2) CDC ArboNET or CDC WNV activity page with California 2024 data; (3) at least one county-level report or press release with case/death counts for August 2024. If these are not found, iteration 2 should target county health departments (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno) and ProMED/news sources directly.
warnings: Upstream queries used rigid exact-phrase matching (e.g., '"WNV California August 2024"') and literal date-range strings that are unlikely to match real agency page titles or report language — these have been replaced with natural-language queries targeting agency names and report types
Peer-reviewed literature queries (q_exec_005, q_exec_006) are deprioritized entirely in iteration 1: a 2024 August single-month window is too recent for published literature to exist

The 10-query total budget across 2 iterations means iteration 1 must be highly targeted; the 4 queries selected cover the two highest-authority source tiers (CDPH, CDC) plus county-level and news channels

If CDPH reports cumulative season-to-date figures rather than monthly breakdowns, the August 2024 window may need to be inferred from week-over-week differences in weekly reports — this should be flagged during extraction
California WNV surveillance may be reported by CDPH as 'year-to-date through [week]' rather than calendar-month totals; extractors should note the reporting period explicitly

count_semantics_notes: CDPH WNV reports typically distinguish neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive human cases; map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed, non-neuroinvasive to cases_probable or cases_confirmed per case definition.
ArboNET uses 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CSTE case definitions: confirmed = lab-confirmed (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable = IgM in serum with compatible illness.
Cumulative season-to-date figures are common; extract the specific August 2024 increment or clearly flag if figures are cumulative YTD.
County-level breakdowns may be available in CDPH weekly WNV updates; prioritize county-level rows over statewide aggregates when both are present.
Death counts in WNV reports may lag case counts by weeks; note reporting lag in evidence_quote.
Sentinel chicken seroconversions and dead bird positives are NOT human case counts; exclude from case_count fields but note in evidence_quote if contextually relevant.
Some CDPH tables report 'human cases' as a combined confirmed+probable figure; record in cases_unspecified if disaggregation is unavailable.
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH WNV updates; record as null if absent rather than zero.
disambiguation_risks: WNV animal/veterinary cases (horses, birds) must not be counted as human cases
Sentinel chicken seroconversions are surveillance indicators, not human cases
Dead bird reports are epizootic indicators, not human cases
Mosquito pool positivity rates are vector data, not human case counts
West Nile virus vs. other California arboviruses (St. Louis encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalomyelitis virus, dengue, Zika) — confirm pathogen identity
Cumulative YTD figures vs. August-specific figures — clearly distinguish time window
WNND (neuroinvasive) vs. WNF (non-neuroinvasive) — do not conflate clinical categories unless source aggregates them
California county names may be ambiguous (e.g., 'Orange' county vs. city of Orange) — always record full county name with 'County' suffix
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates; filter to California-specific rows only

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus weekly or monthly surveillance reports covering August 2024, containing human case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human surveillance in California and publishes weekly WNV activity reports during the transmission season. These are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, and unspecified human case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county and local health department (LHD) WNV situation reports, press releases, or dashboards for August 2024 covering high-burden counties (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno, Kern, San Joaquin, Riverside, San Bernardino).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County-level LHDs often publish localized WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than state-level reports. High-burden California counties are historically the primary contributors to statewide WNV case totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance data for California for 2024, including any state-level or county-level human case and death counts reportable for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case data. CDC DVBD may publish weekly or cumulative WNV maps and tables that include California-specific counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., CDC WNV disease data, ProMED, HealthMap, or open data portals) that aggregate California WNV human case counts for 2024 for cross-validation against CDPH primary sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators provide a held-back validation layer to detect discrepancies in case counts, death totals, or reporting periods between primary and secondary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO or ECDC situation reports or global arboviral surveillance summaries that include United States or California WNV data for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports may independently summarize US WNV activity and provide a secondary validation reference for California case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definitions for West Nile virus confirmed, probable, and suspected human cases to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WNV case definitions distinguish neuroinvasive disease (WNND) from West Nile fever (WNF) and affect how confirmed vs. probable counts should be interpreted and mapped to schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV transmission season patterns, historical burden, and 2024 season context to support interpretation of August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Contextual literature helps assess whether August 2024 counts are within expected seasonal ranges and supports normalization decisions for cumulative vs. incident count semantics.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report cumulative year-to-date WNV counts without a clear August 2024 incident period breakdown, or that mix human and animal/vector surveillance data, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Cumulative YTD counts may not be attributable to the August 2024 window alone. Mixed human/animal data violates the task acceptance contract exclusion terms and must be reviewed before any extraction attempt.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite WNV case counts without a clearly identified primary official source, for human review to assess provenance reliability.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may cite unofficial or unverified counts. Without traceable provenance to an official agency, such records require human review before entering the collection pipeline.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Division of Communicable Disease Control publishes weekly West Nile virus activity reports during the California transmission season (typically May–November), including human case counts by county, disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. fever), deaths, and hospitalizations. California county and city health departments (58 LHDs) may publish localized WNV human case data. CDC DVBD and ArboNET publish state-level human WNV surveillance data. These are the highest-priority extractable sourc...[truncated]

CDC ArboNET structured data tables, CDC WNV disease data open datasets, California open data portals, and HealthMap/ProMED aggregated surveillance databases may provide independently structured California WNV human case counts for cross-validation. These sources are held back from primary extraction and used to validate collection-source records.

WHO, PAHO, and ECDC may publish global or regional arboviral surveillance summaries that include US WNV activity data for 2024. These provide an independent international validation layer for California case and death totals.

Reputable California news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and public health news services (e.g., CIDRAP, ProMED) may report WNV human case counts, deaths, or outbreak alerts for California in August 2024, often citing CDPH or county LHD data. Useful as collection support when official sources are not yet indexed or accessible.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV transmission, case definitions, historical burden, and 2024 season context support interpretation and normalization of extracted counts. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific incident data due to publication lag, but valuable for case definition and count semantics context.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH WNV reports typically distinguish neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive human cases; map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed, non-neuroinvasive to cases_probable or cases_confirmed per case definition.
ArboNET uses 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CSTE case definitions: confirmed = lab-confirmed (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable = IgM in serum with compatible illness.
Cumulative season-to-date figures are common; extract the specific August 2024 increment or clearly flag if figures are cumulative YTD.
County-level breakdowns may be available in CDPH weekly WNV updates; prioritize county-level rows over statewide aggregates when both are present.
Death counts in WNV reports may lag case counts by weeks; note reporting lag in evidence_quote.
Sentinel chicken seroconversions and dead bird positives are NOT human case counts; exclude from case_count fields but note in evidence_quote if contextually relevant.
Some CDPH tables report 'human cases' as a combined confirmed+probable figure; record in cases_unspecified if disaggregation is unavailable.
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH WNV updates; record as null if absent rather than zero.
disambiguation_risks: WNV animal/veterinary cases (horses, birds) must not be counted as human cases
Sentinel chicken seroconversions are surveillance indicators, not human cases
Dead bird reports are epizootic indicators, not human cases
Mosquito pool positivity rates are vector data, not human case counts
West Nile virus vs. other California arboviruses (St. Louis encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalomyelitis virus, dengue, Zika) — confirm pathogen identity
Cumulative YTD figures vs. August-specific figures — clearly distinguish time window
WNND (neuroinvasive) vs. WNF (non-neuroinvasive) — do not conflate clinical categories unless source aggregates them
California county names may be ambiguous (e.g., 'Orange' county vs. city of Orange) — always record full county name with 'County' suffix
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates; filter to California-specific rows only

Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus weekly or monthly surveillance reports covering August 2024, containing human case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human surveillance in California and publishes weekly WNV activity reports during the transmission season. These are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, and unspecified human case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county and local health department (LHD) WNV situation reports, press releases, or dashboards for August 2024 covering high-burden counties (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno, Kern, San Joaquin, Riverside, San Bernardino).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County-level LHDs often publish localized WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than state-level reports. High-burden California counties are historically the primary contributors to statewide WNV case totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance data for California for 2024, including any state-level or county-level human case and death counts reportable for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case data. CDC DVBD may publish weekly or cumulative WNV maps and tables that include California-specific counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., CDC WNV disease data, ProMED, HealthMap, or open data portals) that aggregate California WNV human case counts for 2024 for cross-validation against CDPH primary sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators provide a held-back validation layer to detect discrepancies in case counts, death totals, or reporting periods between primary and secondary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO or ECDC situation reports or global arboviral surveillance summaries that include United States or California WNV data for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports may independently summarize US WNV activity and provide a secondary validation reference for California case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definitions for West Nile virus confirmed, probable, and suspected human cases to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WNV case definitions distinguish neuroinvasive disease (WNND) from West Nile fever (WNF) and affect how confirmed vs. probable counts should be interpreted and mapped to schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV transmission season patterns, historical burden, and 2024 season context to support interpretation of August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Contextual literature helps assess whether August 2024 counts are within expected seasonal ranges and supports normalization decisions for cumulative vs. incident count semantics.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report cumulative year-to-date WNV counts without a clear August 2024 incident period breakdown, or that mix human and animal/vector surveillance data, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Cumulative YTD counts may not be attributable to the August 2024 window alone. Mixed human/animal data violates the task acceptance contract exclusion terms and must be reviewed before any extraction attempt.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite WNV case counts without a clearly identified primary official source, for human review to assess provenance reliability.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may cite unofficial or unverified counts. Without traceable provenance to an official agency, such records require human review before entering the collection pipeline.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Division of Communicable Disease Control publishes weekly West Nile virus activity reports during the California transmission season (typically May–November), including human case counts by county, disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. fever), deaths, and hospitalizations. California county and city health departments (58 LHDs) may publish localized WNV human case data. CDC DVBD and ArboNET publish state-level human WNV surveillance data. These are the highest-priority extractable sourc...[truncated]

CDC ArboNET structured data tables, CDC WNV disease data open datasets, California open data portals, and HealthMap/ProMED aggregated surveillance databases may provide independently structured California WNV human case counts for cross-validation. These sources are held back from primary extraction and used to validate collection-source records.

WHO, PAHO, and ECDC may publish global or regional arboviral surveillance summaries that include US WNV activity data for 2024. These provide an independent international validation layer for California case and death totals.

Reputable California news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and public health news services (e.g., CIDRAP, ProMED) may report WNV human case counts, deaths, or outbreak alerts for California in August 2024, often citing CDPH or county LHD data. Useful as collection support when official sources are not yet indexed or accessible.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV transmission, case definitions, historical burden, and 2024 season context support interpretation and normalization of extracted counts. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific incident data due to publication lag, but valuable for case definition and count semantics context.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance data for California for 2024, including any state-level or county-level human case and death counts reportable for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case data. CDC DVBD may publish weekly or cumulative WNV maps and tables that include California-specific counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., CDC WNV disease data, ProMED, HealthMap, or open data portals) that aggregate California WNV human case counts for 2024 for cross-validation against CDPH primary sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators provide a held-back validation layer to detect discrepancies in case counts, death totals, or reporting periods between primary and secondary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO or ECDC situation reports or global arboviral surveillance summaries that include United States or California WNV data for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports may independently summarize US WNV activity and provide a secondary validation reference for California case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definitions for West Nile virus confirmed, probable, and suspected human cases to support correct classification of extracted counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV transmission season patterns, historical burden, and 2024 season context to support interpretation of August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Contextual literature helps assess whether August 2024 counts are within expected seasonal ranges and supports normalization decisions for cumulative vs. incident count semantics.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report cumulative year-to-date WNV counts without a clear August 2024 incident period breakdown, or that mix human and animal/vector surveillance data, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Cumulative YTD counts may not be attributable to the August 2024 window alone. Mixed human/animal data violates the task acceptance contract exclusion terms and must be reviewed before any extraction attempt.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite WNV case counts without a clearly identified primary official source, for human review to assess provenance reliability.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may cite unofficial or unverified counts. Without traceable provenance to an official agency, such records require human review before entering the collection pipeline.

WHO, PAHO, and ECDC may publish global or regional arboviral surveillance summaries that include US WNV activity data for 2024. These provide an independent international validation layer for California case and death totals.

Reputable California news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and public health news services (e.g., CIDRAP, ProMED) may report WNV human case counts, deaths, or outbreak alerts for California in August 2024, often citing CDPH or county LHD data. trust_considerations: Prefer sources with explicit .gov or .ca.gov domains for case count data
CDPH and CDC are tier-1 authoritative sources; county health departments are tier-2
News articles are acceptable as collection support only if they cite a named official source or agency report with specific numeric figures
Avoid sources that aggregate or repackage data without citing primary agency — these should not be used as primary evidence
CDC ArboNET data may lag real-time by several weeks; CDPH weekly reports are more timely for the August 2024 window

WNV case classification in California follows CDC ArboNET case definitions: neuroinvasive disease (confirmed) vs. non-neuroinvasive (confirmed) vs. probable — queries should surface sources that distinguish these categories

If these are not found, iteration 2 should target county health departments (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno) and ProMED/news sources directly.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH WNV reports typically distinguish neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive human cases; map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed, non-neuroinvasive to cases_probable or cases_confirmed per case definition.
ArboNET uses 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CSTE case definitions: confirmed = lab-confirmed (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable = IgM in serum with compatible illness.
Cumulative season-to-date figures are common; extract the specific August 2024 increment or clearly flag if figures are cumulative YTD.
County-level breakdowns may be available in CDPH weekly WNV updates; prioritize county-level rows over statewide aggregates when both are present.
Death counts in WNV reports may lag case counts by weeks; note reporting lag in evidence_quote.
Sentinel chicken seroconversions and dead bird positives are NOT human case counts; exclude from case_count fields but note in evidence_quote if contextually relevant.
Some CDPH tables report 'human cases' as a combined confirmed+probable figure; record in cases_unspecified if disaggregation is unavailable.
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH WNV updates; record as null if absent rather than zero.
disambiguation_risks: WNV animal/veterinary cases (horses, birds) must not be counted as human cases
Sentinel chicken seroconversions are surveillance indicators, not human cases
Dead bird reports are epizootic indicators, not human cases
Mosquito pool positivity rates are vector data, not human case counts
West Nile virus vs. other California arboviruses (St. Louis encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalomyelitis virus, dengue, Zika) — confirm pathogen identity
Cumulative YTD figures vs. August-specific figures — clearly distinguish time window
WNND (neuroinvasive) vs. WNF (non-neuroinvasive) — do not conflate clinical categories unless source aggregates them
California county names may be ambiguous (e.g., 'Orange' county vs. city of Orange) — always record full county name with 'County' suffix
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates; filter to California-specific rows only

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus weekly or monthly surveillance reports covering August 2024, containing human case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human surveillance in California and publishes weekly WNV activity reports during the transmission season. source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county and local health department (LHD) WNV situation reports, press releases, or dashboards for August 2024 covering high-burden counties (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno, Kern, San Joaquin, Riverside, San Bernardino).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County-level LHDs often publish localized WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than state-level reports. High-burden California counties are historically the primary contributors to statewide WNV case totals.

count_semantics_notes: CDPH WNV reports typically distinguish neuroinvasive vs. non-neuroinvasive human cases; map neuroinvasive to cases_confirmed where lab-confirmed, non-neuroinvasive to cases_probable or cases_confirmed per case definition.
ArboNET uses 'confirmed' and 'probable' per CSTE case definitions: confirmed = lab-confirmed (IgM in CSF, PRNT, or PCR); probable = IgM in serum with compatible illness.
Cumulative season-to-date figures are common; extract the specific August 2024 increment or clearly flag if figures are cumulative YTD.
County-level breakdowns may be available in CDPH weekly WNV updates; prioritize county-level rows over statewide aggregates when both are present.
Death counts in WNV reports may lag case counts by weeks; note reporting lag in evidence_quote.
Sentinel chicken seroconversions and dead bird positives are NOT human case counts; exclude from case_count fields but note in evidence_quote if contextually relevant.
Some CDPH tables report 'human cases' as a combined confirmed+probable figure; record in cases_unspecified if disaggregation is unavailable.
Hospitalization data may not be systematically reported in all CDPH WNV updates; record as null if absent rather than zero.
disambiguation_risks: WNV animal/veterinary cases (horses, birds) must not be counted as human cases
Sentinel chicken seroconversions are surveillance indicators, not human cases
Dead bird reports are epizootic indicators, not human cases
Mosquito pool positivity rates are vector data, not human case counts
West Nile virus vs. other California arboviruses (St. Louis encephalitis virus, Western equine encephalomyelitis virus, dengue, Zika) — confirm pathogen identity
Cumulative YTD figures vs. August-specific figures — clearly distinguish time window
WNND (neuroinvasive) vs. WNF (non-neuroinvasive) — do not conflate clinical categories unless source aggregates them
California county names may be ambiguous (e.g., 'Orange' county vs. city of Orange) — always record full county name with 'County' suffix
ArboNET data may reflect national aggregates; filter to California-specific rows only

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about West Nile Virus Disease.
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH (California Department of Public Health) West Nile virus weekly or monthly surveillance reports covering August 2024, containing human case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDPH is the primary state-level authority for WNV human surveillance in California and publishes weekly WNV activity reports during the transmission season. These are the highest-priority extractable sources for confirmed, probable, and unspecified human case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify California county and local health department (LHD) WNV situation reports, press releases, or dashboards for August 2024 covering high-burden counties (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Fresno, Kern, San Joaquin, Riverside, San Bernardino).
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: County-level LHDs often publish localized WNV human case data earlier or at finer geographic granularity than state-level reports. High-burden California counties are historically the primary contributors to statewide WNV case totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC ArboNET or CDC DVBD West Nile virus surveillance data for California for 2024, including any state-level or county-level human case and death counts reportable for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system and publishes state-level WNV human case data. CDC DVBD may publish weekly or cumulative WNV maps and tables that include California-specific counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent structured databases or dashboards (e.g., CDC WNV disease data, ProMED, HealthMap, or open data portals) that aggregate California WNV human case counts for 2024 for cross-validation against CDPH primary sources.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent aggregators provide a held-back validation layer to detect discrepancies in case counts, death totals, or reporting periods between primary and secondary sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO PAHO or ECDC situation reports or global arboviral surveillance summaries that include United States or California WNV data for August 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International organization reports may independently summarize US WNV activity and provide a secondary validation reference for California case and death totals.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDPH or CDC case definitions for West Nile virus confirmed, probable, and suspected human cases to support correct classification of extracted counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WNV case definitions distinguish neuroinvasive disease (WNND) from West Nile fever (WNF) and affect how confirmed vs. probable counts should be interpreted and mapped to schema fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or epidemiological reports describing California WNV transmission season patterns, historical burden, and 2024 season context to support interpretation of August 2024 case counts.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Contextual literature helps assess whether August 2024 counts are within expected seasonal ranges and supports normalization decisions for cumulative vs. incident count semantics.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that report cumulative year-to-date WNV counts without a clear August 2024 incident period breakdown, or that mix human and animal/vector surveillance data, for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Cumulative YTD counts may not be attributable to the August 2024 window alone. Mixed human/animal data violates the task acceptance contract exclusion terms and must be reviewed before any extraction attempt.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any news or situation report sources that cite WNV case counts without a clearly identified primary official source, for human review to assess provenance reliability.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may cite unofficial or unverified counts. Without traceable provenance to an official agency, such records require human review before entering the collection pipeline.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDPH Division of Communicable Disease Control publishes weekly West Nile virus activity reports during the California transmission season (typically May–November), including human case counts by county, disease classification (neuroinvasive vs. fever), deaths, and hospitalizations. California county and city health departments (58 LHDs) may publish localized WNV human case data. CDC DVBD and ArboNET publish state-level human WNV surveillance data. These are the highest-priority extractable sourc...[truncated]

CDC ArboNET structured data tables, CDC WNV disease data open datasets, California open data portals, and HealthMap/ProMED aggregated surveillance databases may provide independently structured California WNV human case counts for cross-validation. These sources are held back from primary extraction and used to validate collection-source records.

WHO, PAHO, and ECDC may publish global or regional arboviral surveillance summaries that include US WNV activity data for 2024. These provide an independent international validation layer for California case and death totals.

Reputable California news outlets (e.g., Los Angeles Times, Sacramento Bee, San Francisco Chronicle) and public health news services (e.g., CIDRAP, ProMED) may report WNV human case counts, deaths, or outbreak alerts for California in August 2024, often citing CDPH or county LHD data. Useful as collection support when official sources are not yet indexed or accessible.

Peer-reviewed epidemiological studies on California WNV transmission, case definitions, historical burden, and 2024 season context support interpretation and normalization of extracted counts. Unlikely to contain August 2024-specific incident data due to publication lag, but valuable for case definition and count semantics context.

query_batch.query: California Department of Public Health West Nile virus 2024 cases deaths surveillance report
query_batch.query_rationale: CDPH is the primary authoritative source for statewide WNV surveillance in California. Their annual or weekly WNV activity reports will contain confirmed/probable case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and county-level breakdowns for 2024, including the August window. Using agency name + disease + year in natural language is more likely to surface the correct landing page than rigid exact-phrase matching.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDPH West Nile virus surveillance page, annual summary, or weekly activity report for 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdph.ca.gov domain; official state agency authorship; tabular case counts by county and week

query_batch.query: CDC West Nile virus 2024 California cases ArboNET surveillance statistics
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC's ArboNET system is the national arboviral surveillance database and publishes state-level WNV case counts including California. The CDC WNV activity page is updated regularly during transmission season and will contain confirmed neuroinvasive and non-neuroinvasive case counts, deaths, and state breakdowns for 2024. This is a critical cross-validation source against CDPH data.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC WNV activity and surveillance data page or ArboNET state-level table for 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; ArboNET attribution; tabular state-by-state case counts

query_batch.query: West Nile virus California county August 2024 cases deaths public health department report
query_batch.query_rationale: California WNV activity is heavily concentrated in specific counties (Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno, Riverside, San Bernardino). County-level health departments and vector control districts publish their own WNV activity reports and press releases, which may contain locality-level case counts and dates not aggregated in state-level reports. This query targets county-level official sources for August 2024 specifically.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: County public health department press releases, vector control district activity reports, or local health officer advisories for August 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: County .gov or .ca.gov domains; vector control district authorship; dated press releases or activity bulletins

August is peak WNV transmission season in California, making news coverage likely.

query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Dateline August 2024; direct citation of CDPH, county health department, or vector control district figures; named official spokesperson quotes

WNV surveillance reports from CDPH, CDC, and county health departments are published in English. No localization to other languages is needed for this jurisdiction and disease combination. trust_considerations: Prefer sources with explicit .gov or .ca.gov domains for case count data
CDPH and CDC are tier-1 authoritative sources; county health departments are tier-2
News articles are acceptable as collection support only if they cite a named official source or agency report with specific numeric figures
Avoid sources that aggregate or repackage data without citing primary agency — these should not be used as primary evidence
CDC ArboNET data may lag real-time by several weeks; CDPH weekly reports are more timely for the August 2024 window

WNV case classification in California follows CDC ArboNET case definitions: neuroinvasive disease (confirmed) vs. non-neuroinvasive (confirmed) vs. probable — queries should surface sources that distinguish these categories
search_iteration_plans.stop_condition_hypothesis: Iteration 1 is sufficient if results surface: (1) a CDPH WNV surveillance page or weekly/annual report with August 2024 case counts; (2) CDC ArboNET or CDC WNV activity page with California 2024 data; (3) at least one county-level report or press release with case/death counts for August 2024. If these are not found, iteration 2 should target county health departments (e.g., Los Angeles, Sacramento, Kern, Fresno) and ProMED/news sources directly.
warnings: Upstream queries used rigid exact-phrase matching (e.g., '"WNV California August 2024"') and literal date-range strings that are unlikely to match real agency page titles or report language — these have been replaced with natural-language queries targeting agency names and report types
Peer-reviewed literature queries (q_exec_005, q_exec_006) are deprioritized entirely in iteration 1: a 2024 August single-month window is too recent for published literature to exist

The 10-query total budget across 2 iterations means iteration 1 must be highly targeted; the 4 queries selected cover the two highest-authority source tiers (CDPH, CDC) plus county-level and news channels

If CDPH reports cumulative season-to-date figures rather than monthly breakdowns, the August 2024 window may need to be inferred from week-over-week differences in weekly reports — this should be flagged during extraction
California WNV surveillance may be reported by CDPH as 'year-to-date through [week]' rather than calendar-month totals; extractors should note the reporting period explicitly
